title: Secure and Compliant Data Design: IAM, Encryption, Residency and Environments

concepts.heading: Identities and Least Privilege for Pipelines
concepts.body: Every pipeline runs as an identity, and the safe default is not the one Google Cloud hands you. A Dataflow job has a submitting user and a worker service account, the account the worker VMs use to read sources and write sinks. By default that is the Compute Engine default service account, which is shared and often over-privileged. Google recommends a user-managed worker service account per pipeline, holding roles/dataflow.worker plus data roles granted on the narrowest resource: the one bucket it reads and the one dataset it writes, not the project. In BigQuery, who may read data and where a query runs are separate decisions. A marketing group that must query the central team's dataset but pay for its own queries gets Data Viewer on that dataset in the data project and Job User in the marketing project: no copies, no write access, clean chargeback. Basic roles and organization-wide admin roles are the opposite of this pattern.

concepts.heading: Projects, Zones and Environments
concepts.body: The project is the unit for IAM scope, quotas, billing, audit logs and organization policy inheritance, so it is the main governance boundary for data. A retailer with raw partner files, curated finance data and a data science group experimenting with copies should not use one project and one dataset, because project-level Data Editor would let an experiment change finance tables. The usual layout separates zones (raw, curated, consumption, sandbox) and environments (dev, test, prod) into different projects grouped in folders, with roles granted to groups at the dataset or bucket level. Dev versus prod applies to pipeline code too. Dataform compiles SQL workflows through release configurations and schedules them through workflow configurations, and a workflow configuration can run as a dedicated service account. Developers keep dev workspaces, while scheduled production runs use an identity no one signs in with; acting as that account needs iam.serviceAccounts.actAs, which is granted sparingly.

concepts.heading: Encryption Keys and Data Residency
concepts.body: Residency has two halves: where data is stored and where it is processed. Placement is fixed early. A BigQuery dataset has a location chosen at creation, and a load job needs its Cloud Storage bucket in the same location, so an EU dataset fed from a us-central1 bucket fails until the files move to an EU location; moving the dataset to the US would break the rule. The resource locations organization policy constraint is the guardrail, and Google recommends an in: value group such as in:eu-locations so new EU locations are covered. Set at an organization or folder, it is inherited by projects teams create later. Dataflow handles job metadata and controls workers in the region you pick, so choose an EU region. For customer-managed encryption keys, a Cloud KMS key ring has a fixed location and Google documents that it should match the dataset location: an EU multi-region dataset gets a key ring in europe. The key lives in one place and cannot be moved.

concepts.heading: Protecting Values, Boundaries and Evidence
concepts.body: Sensitive Data Protection (formerly Cloud DLP) de-identifies values with tokenization. Deterministic encryption (AES-SIV) and format-preserving encryption (FPE-FFX) are reversible with the Cloud KMS key and give equal inputs equal tokens, so analysts can still join customer and order tables while only the fraud service holds decrypt rights on the key. FPE keeps a 16-digit card number 16 digits long, which suits a nightly test refresh whose application validates the format. Hashing is one-way. For column and row control inside BigQuery, use column-level policy tags for national ID values and row-level access policies for regions. IAM cannot say that data must not leave a boundary; VPC Service Controls draws a perimeter that blocks copying query results to a project outside it. For evidence, BigQuery writes Data Access audit logs by default, and a log sink exports them to a separate audit project or bucket for multi-year retention.

examPoints: A question that gives a Dataflow job the default Compute Engine service account and asks for least privilege points to a user-managed worker service account with roles on the single bucket and dataset.
A question about an EU dataset, a key ring location or a bucket in another region points to matching locations everywhere, with a resource locations policy as the guardrail.
A question where analysts may read data but must not copy it out, or must join on IDs they cannot see, points to VPC Service Controls or Sensitive Data Protection tokenization with a KMS key.

quiz.q: A health-data company must keep a BigQuery dataset in the EU multi-region and encrypt every table with a customer-managed key. Where should the Cloud KMS key ring be created?
choices: In the europe multi-region, so that the key ring location matches the dataset location
In the us multi-region, because the key ring location is independent of the dataset location
In the global location, so one key ring can protect datasets that sit in any region
In any single EU region, because a region key ring can protect a multi-region dataset
quiz.explain: BigQuery guidance is to create the key ring in a location that matches the dataset, and an EU multi-region dataset matches the europe location. A global key ring is tempting for flexibility, but it does not match the dataset and weakens a residency argument.

quiz.q: A payments company copies customer and order tables into BigQuery. Analysts must join them on customer ID without ever seeing the real IDs, while a small fraud service must recover the real ID for flagged cases. Which design fits?
choices: Replace each ID with a fixed text value so that analysts can never reach the original values
Hash each ID one-way with a salt and keep the salt in a table that only analysts can read
Tokenize each ID with deterministic encryption and give only the fraud service key access
Encrypt each ID with a different random key per row and store those keys beside the data
quiz.explain: Deterministic encryption gives equal IDs equal tokens, so joins still work, and IAM on the Cloud KMS key controls who can re-identify. A fixed replacement is tempting for secrecy, but it collapses every join into one value.

recap: Run pipelines as least-privilege service accounts, separate zones and environments by project, match locations for datasets, buckets, jobs and keys under a resource locations policy, and use tokenization, perimeters and audit sinks to protect and prove access.

title: Reliable Pipelines: Validation, Monitoring, Disaster Recovery and Consistency

concepts.heading: Validating and Cleaning Data in the Pipeline
concepts.body: Fidelity means bad data is caught, kept for review and never silently loaded. In Dataform, an assertion is a query that returns violating rows, and the run fails if any come back. Built-in conditions in a table's config cover nonNull, uniqueKey and rowConditions, so missing customer IDs and duplicate order IDs are tested on every run. Unit tests are different: they mock an action's inputs and compare the SQL output, so null handling and regular-expression edge cases are checked before release. Use unit tests for logic and assertions for the data that arrives. In Dataflow, an uncaught exception in a DoFn retries the bundle four times in batch and then fails, but retries indefinitely in streaming and can stall the job, so the code catches the error and sends the record to a dead-letter destination such as a BigQuery table or Pub/Sub topic. Cloud Data Fusion gives a no-code route: an error collector gathers rejected records into a separate sink for review.

concepts.heading: Observing and Hardening Orchestration
concepts.body: Pipelines fail at night, so the design decides who finds out. Cloud Composer (Managed Service for Apache Airflow in current product pages) sends scheduler, worker, database and DAG-run metrics to Cloud Monitoring and logs to Cloud Logging, and alerting policies on them notify people as failures happen instead of when business users complain. Resilience has two layers. For infrastructure, a highly resilient environment runs the metadata database as a high-availability instance and spreads Airflow components across zones, so losing a zone does not stop scheduling. For workflow design, tasks use retries and retry_delay in default_args so transient API errors heal themselves. Retries are safe only when tasks are idempotent. A nightly append that reruns after a timeout and doubles the rows is a design flaw, not an orchestrator flaw. The fix is to load into a staging table and apply a MERGE on the business key, or overwrite the day's partition, so any rerun converges to the same result.

concepts.heading: Fault Tolerance and Disaster Recovery for Stored Data
concepts.body: Match the recovery tool to the failure. A BigQuery multi-region does not keep data available if a physical region is destroyed, so it is not regional redundancy. For a requirement to keep reporting within minutes after a regional outage, use managed disaster recovery: cross-region dataset replication plus an Enterprise Plus edition reservation, which includes standby compute in the paired region. A soft failover waits for pending changes to replicate and needs both regions, so it fits planned tests. A hard failover promotes the secondary immediately and can lose unreplicated data. Logical damage and retention are different problems. Time travel covers a window of 2 to 7 days, and fail-safe adds seven more for emergency recovery. Table snapshots keep month-end versions for a year while storing only the changed bytes. For raw files in a Cloud Storage dual-region bucket, default replication targets 99.9% of new objects within an hour; turbo replication targets a 15-minute RPO for all objects.

concepts.heading: Consistency, Transactions and Availability Trade-offs
concepts.body: Distributed stores trade strictness for reach, and the stem's wording tells you which side matters. A global ledger where two stores update the same item at once, with no double counting or reordering, calls for Spanner, whose external consistency makes transactions behave as if run one at a time in real-time order, even across regions. Bigtable replication between clusters is eventually consistent. A rider app that reads back a just-written pickup point and sometimes sees the old value is fixed with single-cluster routing in the app profile, which gives read-your-writes consistency while the other cluster stays a replica; multi-cluster routing favors availability instead. Inside BigQuery, a staging-to-history move with separate statements can leave rows in both tables after a failure. A multi-statement transaction commits or rolls back all changes together, with snapshot isolation. Reordering the statements only changes whether a crash causes duplicates or loss.

examPoints: A question that wants bad rows caught on every run and kept for review points to Dataform assertions, a Dataflow dead-letter output or a Data Fusion error collector, depending on the tool in the stem.

A question that asks for reporting within minutes after a regional loss, with a multi-region dataset already in place, points to BigQuery managed disaster recovery, since a multi-region is not regional redundancy.
A question about a retry that duplicates rows points to idempotent loads with MERGE, and one about two tables changing together points to a multi-statement transaction.

quiz.q: A streaming Dataflow pipeline parses JSON events in a DoFn and writes to BigQuery. After one malformed record arrives, the job stops making progress and the same exception repeats. What is the best fix?
choices: Catch the parsing error in the DoFn and emit the bad record to a dead-letter destination for later inspection
Switch the job to batch mode, because batch stops retrying a failing bundle after a fixed number of attempts
Increase the worker count, because more workers will spread the failing bundle across additional machines
Raise the Pub/Sub acknowledgement deadline so that the failing message is redelivered less often to workers
quiz.explain: In streaming mode a failing bundle is retried indefinitely, so the code must handle the exception and route the record aside. Switching to batch is tempting, but batch simply fails the whole pipeline after its retries.

quiz.q: A ride-hailing app keeps trip state in Bigtable replicated across two regions. Right after a rider changes a pickup point, the app reads it back and sometimes sees the old value. Availability during a regional outage matters too. What should the team change?
choices: Move the table to BigQuery, because it offers stronger consistency for single-row lookups than Bigtable
Use multi-cluster routing, because requests then reach the nearest cluster, which always holds the newest value
Add a third cluster, because a larger replica set makes replication between clusters complete sooner
Use single-cluster routing in the app profile and change the profile to the other cluster on failover
quiz.explain: Single-cluster routing gives read-your-writes consistency, and failover becomes a deliberate profile change. Multi-cluster routing is tempting for availability, but replication between clusters is eventually consistent.

recap: Test data with assertions, dead letters and error collectors, alert on orchestrators and make tasks idempotent, pick the recovery tool for the failure (managed DR, snapshots, turbo replication), and choose consistency models by what the application cannot tolerate.

title: Flexible and Portable Designs: Requirements, Open Formats, Multi-cloud and Staging

concepts.heading: From Requirements to Architecture
concepts.body: A good design starts by turning each quantified requirement into a property the architecture must have. Seconds of latency points to streaming ingestion and processing rather than periodic batch. Spiky, unpredictable volume points to a buffer that absorbs bursts, Pub/Sub, and workers that autoscale, Dataflow. A small team with no cluster management points to serverless parts. Analytical dashboards point to BigQuery as the sink. A ticketing company that sees quiet days and sudden on-sale spikes, and wants sales on a dashboard within seconds, lands on exactly this pattern. When existing code is the main requirement, the answer changes: about 200 nightly Spark jobs with custom JARs, to be moved within a quarter with minimal change, fit Dataproc, which runs open source Spark and Hadoop. Dataflow, BigQuery SQL and Data Fusion are later modernization targets because each needs the logic rewritten into a different model. The wording of the constraint chooses the service.

concepts.heading: Open Formats and Open Programming Models
concepts.body: Lock-in comes from proprietary formats and proprietary programming models, so portability is built from open ones. Dataflow is a managed runner for Apache Beam pipelines, and Beam separates the pipeline definition from the runner, so the same logic can run on Dataflow, Apache Flink or Apache Spark. Keep transformation logic in Beam transforms and use Beam I/O connectors; the thin service-specific glue is easy to replace. For data, self-describing typed formats such as Avro, Parquet and ORC are read natively by BigQuery, Dataflow and Spark, whereas CSV carries no types and breaks when columns change. Avro suits write-heavy landing zones because a new field with a default value can be added safely. When both a BigQuery team (SQL DML) and a Spark team need the same tables, Apache Iceberg managed tables in BigQuery keep one copy in buckets you own, with Iceberg metadata that Spark and other engines can read. Writes go through BigQuery.

concepts.heading: Multi-cloud and Storage Decoupling
concepts.body: Sometimes data cannot or should not be copied. A retailer whose clickstream must stay in an AWS region can still join it with BigQuery sales tables. BigQuery Omni runs BigQuery compute in AWS or Azure regions, and BigLake tables over Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage are queried in place through a connection. In an Omni join the filtering happens in the AWS region and only the subquery result crosses over, so raw objects never move and no copy job is needed. Omni needs no cluster to run and no copy job to schedule. The same decoupling helps migrations from Hadoop. HDFS ties data to machines, so you keep the machines to keep the data. On Google Cloud, store the data in Cloud Storage, read it from Spark through the Cloud Storage connector, and create short-lived Dataproc clusters per job. Object storage has higher per-operation latency, which is acceptable for batch jobs that run monthly.

concepts.heading: Staging Zones, Cataloging and Profiling
concepts.body: A layered layout keeps designs flexible. A raw (landing) zone holds source files exactly as received on cheap object storage and is the system of record. A curated zone holds validated, standardized data, and serving tables feed consumers. A logistics company whose cleaning rules change several times a year can rebuild curated tables from raw without asking partners to resend files, and with versioned transformation code it can reproduce a table as it was a year ago. Cleaning that discards information at ingest makes both impossible. Metadata makes the layers usable. Knowledge Catalog (renamed from Dataplex Universal Catalog in April 2026; API, CLI and IAM names unchanged) catalogs the assets, and a data profile scan analyzes a BigQuery table to produce statistics about its columns. Scans can run on a schedule or on demand, and the results can be used to recommend data quality rules. Profile first, then decide what to validate.

examPoints: A question that asks for the same pipeline logic to run on Flink or Spark later points to Apache Beam on Dataflow, because the programming model is what is portable.

A question where data must stay in S3 or Blob Storage yet join BigQuery tables points to BigQuery Omni with BigLake tables, and a question about one copy shared by SQL and Spark points to Iceberg managed tables.
A question about changing business rules and re-deriving past tables points to a raw landing zone plus versioned transformations, and one about moving existing Spark jobs quickly points to Dataproc.

quiz.q: A bank wants to limit lock-in without giving up managed services for a new analytics platform. Which choice best supports portability of both its data and its processing logic?
choices: Write transformations as BigQuery stored procedures only, and keep the landing files as a vendor-specific binary export
Write pipelines with Apache Beam and land data in open columnar or row formats such as Parquet or Avro
Write transformations in the visual designer of one product, and store the landing files as compressed text archives
Write pipelines in service-specific templates and keep the data only in managed tables with no file exports
quiz.explain: Open programming models keep logic independent of the runner, and open formats can be read by many engines. Stored procedures are tempting for simplicity, but they tie logic to one product and a binary export needs its producer to read it.

quiz.q: A retailer's raw clickstream files sit in Amazon S3 and contractually must stay in that AWS region (only query results may leave). Analysts already use BigQuery and want to join the clickstream with BigQuery sales tables without copy jobs. What should they use?
choices: Storage Transfer Service to copy the objects into Cloud Storage nightly, then load them into BigQuery
A Dataflow batch job that reads the S3 objects and writes aggregates into a BigQuery table every hour
A BigQuery load job that points at the S3 bucket and copies the objects into native storage each night
BigQuery Omni with BigLake tables over the S3 data, joined to the sales tables in one query
quiz.explain: Omni runs BigQuery compute next to the data and moves only the subquery result, so the raw objects stay in the AWS region. Transfer tools are tempting for analytics, but every copy-based design moves the files out.

recap: Map each quantified requirement to an architectural property, choose open formats and Beam for portability, query data in place with Omni when it cannot move, decouple storage from compute, and keep a raw zone so curated data can be rebuilt.

title: Planning and Validating Migrations: Databases, Warehouses, Files and Replication

concepts.heading: Choosing the Service: Migrate, Replicate or Schedule a Load
concepts.body: Three services are easy to confuse, and the stem's verbs tell them apart. Database Migration Service (DMS) moves a database into Cloud SQL or AlloyDB and makes the destination the new primary. A continuous migration does an initial dump and load, keeps replicating changes with change data capture while the source stays live, and you promote the destination at cutover, so a 2 TB MySQL system that tolerates only minutes of downtime fits. A one-time migration is a point-in-time snapshot with no writes to the source while it runs, so a 40 GB PostgreSQL database with a weekend of accepted downtime needs nothing more. Datastream is serverless change data capture and replication: it reads logs from sources such as Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server with minimal load, backfills, then streams changes to BigQuery or Cloud Storage while the source stays the system of record. BigQuery Data Transfer Service runs scheduled, managed loads into BigQuery.

concepts.heading: Datastream, Transfer Service Gaps and Private Networking
concepts.body: Datastream writes to BigQuery in one of two modes. Merge mode keeps the destination mirroring the source's current state and applies updates and deletes, which relies on a primary key at the source. Append-only mode adds every change event as a new row, with a datastream_metadata column for ordering, so a compliance team that must reconstruct a row at any past moment wants append-only. Networking is part of the design. If an on-premises Oracle database is reachable only over Cloud VPN from a private network, a public connection profile cannot connect and exposing the listener to the internet breaks the security policy. Create a private connectivity configuration so Datastream reaches the source through VPC peering over the VPN or Interconnect. BigQuery Data Transfer Service loads from sources such as Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, Cloud Storage, Teradata, Redshift, Snowflake and SaaS applications. If a daily run failed for three days, request a backfill run for the missed dates on the same configuration.

concepts.heading: Moving Files: Online Transfer or Transfer Appliance
concepts.body: For files, compare transfer time (size divided by usable bandwidth) with the deadline. Storage Transfer Service is built for large online moves: from on-premises file systems through self-hosted agents, from Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage with Google-managed workers, and from HDFS. It can be scheduled, copies only new or changed data, validates integrity and lets the network team control bandwidth. A manufacturer with 600 TB, a 10 Gbps Interconnect and a nightly sync requirement, or an advertising firm with 150 TB in S3, fits it with nothing to build. A custom Dataflow copier would reimplement listing, retries and checksums. When the numbers do not work, use Transfer Appliance. A remote lab with 800 TB and a shared 200 Mbps link would need more than a year online. You copy data to the encrypted appliance, ship it back, and Google uploads it to your bucket and wipes it. Data size and available bandwidth decide, not downstream design details.

concepts.heading: Migrating Warehouses and Proving the Result
concepts.body: A warehouse migration has code and data, and each needs proof. The BigQuery Migration Service covers the phases: assessment of the existing estate, SQL translation from supported dialects into GoogleSQL (batch, interactive and API translators), data transfer through BigQuery Data Transfer Service, and a data validation tool that checks that source and destination tables match after migration. A retailer moving a Teradata warehouse with thousands of dialect scripts needs both translation and validation; translating code without proving the data, or the reverse, is a common cause of failed cutovers. The wider planning pattern is the same for any migration: decide whether downtime is acceptable, choose online or offline movement from size and bandwidth, plan private connectivity for sources that cannot be exposed, and define how correctness is verified before users switch. For existing Spark or Hadoop code, a lift-and-shift to Dataproc comes first, modernization later.

examPoints: A question where the old database must be live until cutover, with only minutes of downtime, points to a continuous Database Migration Service migration, and a tolerated weekend outage points to a one-time migration.
A question that keeps an operational database in place yet needs changes in BigQuery within seconds points to Datastream, with append-only mode when the full change history must be kept.
A question that compares terabytes against a slow or shared link points to the transfer-time calculation: Storage Transfer Service when it fits, Transfer Appliance when it does not.

quiz.q: An insurer's Oracle database stays on premises as the system of record. Analysts need every change in BigQuery within seconds, without adding noticeable load to the source. Which service fits?
choices: Database Migration Service with a one-time migration, repeated each night to refresh the BigQuery tables
BigQuery Data Transfer Service scheduled hourly, loading full copies of the source tables into BigQuery
Datastream reading the database logs and streaming an initial backfill plus changes to BigQuery
Transfer Appliance shipped to the data center, then reloaded after each batch of changes at the source
quiz.explain: Datastream is serverless change data capture that reads logs with minimal source impact and keeps the source in place. Database Migration Service is tempting because it also uses replication, but it makes a Cloud SQL or AlloyDB database the new primary.

quiz.q: A genomics lab at a remote site has 800 TB of files and a shared 200 Mbps internet link. The data must reach Cloud Storage within two months. Which approach is the best fit?
choices: Run Storage Transfer Service with agents on site, because it validates integrity and can repeat on a schedule
Use Transfer Appliance, copy locally, ship it to Google and let Google upload the data to the bucket
Write a Dataflow pipeline that uploads the files in parallel to the bucket through the shared link
Buy a larger internet plan and compress every file first, then upload it directly to the bucket
quiz.explain: Even a fully dedicated 200 Mbps link would need over a year for 800 TB, so offline shipping removes the network from the critical path. Storage Transfer Service is tempting for its features, but it still depends on the same link.

recap: Pick DMS to move a database, Datastream to replicate changes, BigQuery Data Transfer Service to schedule loads, and Storage Transfer Service or Transfer Appliance by comparing size with bandwidth, with private connectivity and a validation step planned in.
